# Decouple the storyline doc-drift guard from engine-owned heading text

**Headline:** `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` AC5b pins literal Markdown headings of the engine-owned reference `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (a git submodule that dev builds advance to the engine's latest dev tip), so any engine-side heading rename silently reddens this game's unit suite. Replace the heading pins with semantic anchors (API symbols, link resolution) plus a rename-tolerant section-structure check, and document why headings are not a cross-repo contract.

discovered-from: MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L

## Problem statement

Dev builds (`npm run build` → `engine:sync`) compose the **latest** engine dev tip via `git submodule update --remote core`, not the pinned release SHA. When core (dev tip `01d6bcc1`) renamed `## Engine adapter` → `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` in `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, the game's doc-drift guard (AC5b) reddened on **every** dev build, for **every** game repo that pins those headings — even though nothing in Main Street changed. The inline fix (commit `9f2c6185`) asserted the new heading, but the underlying coupling remains: a heading is an implementation detail of the engine's prose, not a contract the game depends on.

## Users / user stories

- As a **Main Street developer**, when I bump or dev-sync the engine, I want `npm test` to fail only for genuine breakage, so a green suite is trustworthy and a red suite means something real.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the doc guard to still fail loudly if the engine reference the game's adapters link to disappears or stops documenting the seam API, so releases cannot silently ship against vanished docs.
- As the **producer/operator**, I want the cross-repo doc dependency to be explicit and cheap to maintain, so a rename is a no-op (or a documented one-line change), not a cross-repo firefight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No literal engine heading pins.** The AC5b block in `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` no longer asserts literal section-heading text of `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`; instead it asserts the semantic anchors the game genuinely depends on: the core reference exists, documents `createStorylineSystem` and the `@story-line` package, and names the `GymStorylineScene` consumer (any of these removed → guard fails).
- **AC2 — Rename tolerance is proven by a fixture test.** A new unit test in the same file feeds a fixture copy of the core doc with section headings renamed (e.g. `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` → `## Renamed seam section`) and asserts the contract check still passes; a negative fixture (missing `createStorylineSystem`) asserts the check still fails. *Metric: run the two fixture cases — tolerance passes, regression fails.*
- **AC3 — Link resolution preserved.** The guard keeps asserting that `docs/game/storylines.md` links to `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and that the target resolves on disk, and that the core reference is linked from `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `core/docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`.
- **AC4 — Failure messages and rationale.** Any guard failure names the offending file and the missing anchor, and the test header comment explains that engine doc headings are not a cross-repo contract (with a pointer to this work item); a corresponding one-line note is added near the "thin adapters" paragraph of `docs/game/storylines.md` and in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (Tests section) so the next engineer does not re-pin headings.
- **AC5 — Engine-revision tolerant and suite green.** The changed test scope passes with the submodule at the pinned SHA and with the engine dev tip the build composes; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- Game-side change only — do **not** edit files inside `core/` (engine-owned submodule, re-scaffolded by the game-repo scaffold); if an engine-side fix is later chosen, it is an engine-repo (CG) work item.
- Do not weaken the guard into a no-op: negative cases (missing file, missing symbol, broken link) must still fail the suite.
- No new dependencies; keep the guard in plain vitest + `node:fs`, consistent with the file's existing style.
- Do not change `configs/engine-pin.json` or the `core` gitlink as part of this work (they already agree at dev HEAD: pin `9ee194e009f5fade0bbbc141c03087d88bf373ef` == gitlink `9ee194e0`).

## Existing state

- Guard: `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, AC5b block asserts `['## API', '## Authoring seams', '## UI adapter', '## Gym demo']` against `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (created by MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY / MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR; heading pin baked in by commit `9f2c6185`).
- Engine doc at current pin (`9ee194e0`) has sections: API, Validation, Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author), UI adapter, Gym demo, Testing.
- The engine repo currently has **no** docs-consistency test and **no** heading anchor manifest (verified: no engine tests reference `docs/core-engine`, no anchor file) — so "engine owns the contract" would be net-new engine work.
- Sibling churn pattern already fixed inline: MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (pin/pointer mismatch when dev sync advances the submodule during a build).

## Desired change

1. Refactor the AC5b assertions into a small pure helper `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc: string, headers: {file: string; link: boolean}): string[]` (returns missing anchors), so the same logic runs against the real file and against fixtures.
2. Replace the `['## API', …]` heading pins with: file-exists + `createStorylineSystem`/`@story-line`/`GymStorylineScene` presence + a structural check that the doc "documents the section topics" without pinning exact heading text (e.g. each required topic keyword found somewhere in the doc, tolerant of heading renames).
3. Add fixture-driven tests for rename tolerance (pass) and missing-symbol regression (fail).
4. Update the test header comment + the two doc notes (AC4).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — AC5b block rewrite, tolerance/regression fixture tests, header rationale.
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/storyline-core-doc-renamed-heading.md` (new) — fixture mirroring the current core doc with headings renamed; or an inline string fixture to avoid duplicating a 400-line doc. Prefer the smallest fixture that provably exercises the renames; if inline, note that it must be refreshed on engine doc content changes.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — one-line note that the guard asserts semantic anchors, not engine heading text.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — one-line note under "Tests" about the engine-doc heading non-contract.
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` gitlink — read-only references; must not be edited here.

## Related work

- MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR — created AC5b ("Storyline docs and drift guards", completed).
- MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY — canonical docs + doc-drift guard (completed).
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — browser-wait soak child where this was discovered (completed).
- MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F — sibling pin/pointer churn from dev-sync submodule advance (completed) — same root-cause class.
- MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV — open sibling that makes the composed engine explicit and fails when worktree `./core` lags the pin (complementary: this item makes the guard tolerant of the composed engine's docs).
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED — origin of dev-sync-on-build policy (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** the more thorough option — "the cross-repo doc contract should be owned by the engine (stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest)" — is deliberately **out of scope** here: it is net-new engine (CG) work affecting every game repo, and it is a producer decision. It is recorded as an open question in the Appendix; if approved, file a separate CG work item. This item stays game-side and is a prerequisite/valid regardless of that decision.
- **Assumption:** semantic symbols (`createStorylineSystem`, `@story-line`, `GymStorylineScene`) are stable markers of the seam API the game links to; the tolerance fixture must keep the renamed headings under the current section topics so it stays representative.
- **Risk — over-loosening:** a rename-tolerant check can drift into a no-op. Mitigated by AC2's negative fixture and AC3's link-resolution assertions.
- **Assumption:** dev builds keep composing the engine dev tip (policy from MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED); the guard must therefore tolerate any dev-tip doc revision.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (2026-10-25): "Should the cross-repo doc contract be owned by the engine (e.g. a stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest), rather than pinned by game tests?" — **OPEN QUESTION** — routed to producer for decision; **Recommended:** keep this item game-side (semantic anchors + rename tolerance), and file the engine-owned-contract option as a separate engine-repo (CG) work item only if the producer opts in — rationale: a heading is an implementation detail of engine prose, not a contract; semantic API symbols plus link resolution cover what games genuinely depend on, and any engine-side contract is net-new engine work hitting every game repo. Source: work-item description ("Follow-up worth deciding…"), research: engine repo has no docs-consistency test and no anchor manifest today; game repo cannot edit `core/`.
- Q2 (2026-10-25): "Should this item also fix the pin/pointer churn class (dev-sync advancing the submodule during builds)?" — Answer (triage): No — that is MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (already fixed inline) / MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV (open); linked as related work above. Source: work-item + worklog search.

## Review log

- Finished completeness review: problem statement, ACs, constraints and key files added; no changes needed after first pass beyond adding the fixture strategy note.
- Finished capture-fidelity review: no user answers given (seed context + repo research only); Q1 recorded as OPEN QUESTION with recommendation.
- Finished related-work review: linked MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR, MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY, MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L, MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F, MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV, MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED; find-related report appended automatically.
- Finished risks & assumptions review: over-loosening mitigated by negative fixtures; engine-contract option isolated as scope-creep item.
- Finished polish & handoff: tightened wording; headline finalised.

## Related work (automated report from find-related)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F** – dev HEAD pin/pointer mismatch: engine-pin.json 01d6bcc1 vs core gitlink d907af9f (completed)
- **MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV** – Worktree core submodule checkouts lag the pin, so test runs compose a stale engine (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: adapter, asserts, author, authoring, broke, browser, build, child, composes, contract, core, cross, delivery, dev, discovered, doc, docs, drift, engine, every, exported, follow, game, handled, heading, inline, latest, line, main, manifest, new, now, npm, old, owned, pin, pinned, pins, pointer, ran, rather, record, red, rename, repo, run, seam, seams, section, should, silently, since, stable, story, storylines, street, submodule, suite, sync, test, tests, tip, unit, validator, wait, whether, worth
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: adapter, author, authoring, browser, build, child, composes, contract, core, cross, dev, discovered, doc, docs, drift, engine, every, follow, game, handled, latest, line, main, manifest, new, now, npm, old, owned, pin, pins, ran, rather, record, red, repo, run, seam, seams, section, should, silently, stable, story, storylines, street, submodule, suite, sync, test, tests, unit, validator, wait, whether, worth

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation
   completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round
   — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned,
   income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category
   (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins /
   reputation / score. The next shared day does **not** start until the player
   clicks **[ Next Turn ]**. Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven
   paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive
   close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on
   `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so
   every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the
   single-player ledger. Additions are optional/backwards-compatible —
   `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the
   headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the
   Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive
   scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours);
   **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an
   explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that
   MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay
   conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in
   `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`,
   `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in
   the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing
   and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the
   engine/headless close path. Checkpoint save ordering
   (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged; the
   dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for
   owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode
   browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated**
   (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing section and the end-of-turn
   summary section, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test
   suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,
  intake_complete) — ordering constraint.
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item (shared with
  single-player panel).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on Game Over; consumes the same per-turn ledger data
  (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's `closingSummary` / shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` + `MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0` (completed) — competitive
  per-seat income choreography and per-seat animated closing: the cadence this
  panel extends; `TurnResult.playerIncome` originates here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`
  reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (round = day):** "one panel per completed round" maps to one
  panel per completed shared day (every seat finished + closing ran); the
  engine has no separate round concept. Recorded from repo evidence; if a
  day-vs-round distinction exists conceptually (e.g. a preset defining round
  length), the panel cadence would need revisiting — flagged for implementer
  verification.
- **Assumption (single human seat):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one
  device, so a blocking dialog on the human's **[ Next Turn ]** cannot stall
  other humans; multifloored safety holds for the current product shape.
  (If networked multiplayer ever lands, blocking semantics need a per-seat
  pause protocol.)
- **Risk (parent not landed):** the owner-keyed ledger this item consumes does
  not exist yet; if the parent lands without the per-seat expense capture
  (today `void`/log-only), this item must extend it — keep additions optional
  and guarded so `presentCompetitiveClosing` and headless/Monte-Carlo flows are
  byte-stable when absent.
- **Risk (blocking regresses headless pacing):** the gate must live in the
  scene presentation tail only (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`), never in engine
  close functions; Monte-Carlo / AI headless days never touch the scene and
  must continue to auto-advance under `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
- **Risk (eliminated seats):** the closing already omits eliminated seats from
  `playerIncome`; the panel must render exactly the seats the closing surfaced
  (no ghost rows for bankrupt/eliminated seats) and say so in its test.
- **Risk (loans are per-owner):** the shared disabled Bank Loan seam is a
  single hook today; when MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands, competitive loans are
  likely per-seat — keep the seam shaped so it can become
  `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` without re-plumbing the panel.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-round history across days (post-game stats,
  MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), networked multiplayer, live loans
  (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) and any round-summary log/graph features are outside
  this item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Blocking behaviour — in single-player the dialog blocks the next-day
  advance until [ Next Turn ] is clicked; in competitive the day currently
  auto-advances after the closing presentation. Options: A) Block like
  single-player — next day starts only after [ Next Turn ]. B) Non-blocking —
